core.title: Make every train structurally valid
core.given: A train definition or registry entry is in scope for the plan (new or existing).
core.when: The planner authors, edits, reviews or validates that train, whatever field is touched.
core.then: The train passes all seven structural validation checks: typed train id in the profiled train URN shape, category declared as a field, the declared spec artifact exists, participants declared, valid dependencies, sequence artifacts named in the profiled artifact-reference form, themes declared.
prefer: Write the train id in the stack's typed train URN shape.
Declare the train's category in its own field with one of nominal|error|alternate|exception.
Make sure a spec artifact exists at the train's declared location (create it or fix the declared location).
List every participant the train uses in its participants list.
Point every dependency at an existing, valid train id.
Name every artifact in the train's sequence in the plan's artifact-reference form.
Declare every theme the train uses in its themes list.
avoid: Untyped or free-form train ids that do not match the profiled train URN shape.
Encoding the category as a digit inside the train identity.
Declaring a spec location that has no artifact behind it.
Using participants, themes or dependencies that are not declared / do not resolve.
Sequence artifacts not in the profiled artifact-reference form.
Treating any of the seven checks as optional or advisory.
core.why: Trains are consumed mechanically by the registry and validators; a train that breaks any structural rule cannot be addressed, resolved or checked reliably.
evidence: Train id matches the profiled train URN shape.
No digit-encoded category in the identity; category field present with value in {nominal, error, alternate, exception}.
A spec artifact exists at the train's declared location.
Every participant referenced is in the participants list.
Every dependency resolves to a valid train id.
Every sequence artifact matches the profiled artifact-reference form.
Every theme used is declared in the themes list.
verification: Strict disposition: a train fails if any one of the seven structural checks fails; none of the checks is optional or advisory.
The check applies to every in-scope train, including existing unchanged trains; it is not gated on a field-level diff.
The spec-artifact existence check relies on the train registry convention, which must enforce spec-file existence.
Activation signal precedence: task-term matches alone do not prove train-authoring intent; the file-kind signal (train definition or registry entry) is primary.

values: existing train in scope for validation

fires: Planner creates a new train definition or registry entry.
Planner edits any field of an existing train (id, category, spec location, participants, dependencies, sequence, themes, or prose) while the train is in scope.
Planner reviews or validates existing trains in the plan, even without changing them.
doesNotFire: Edits to wagons, WMBTs or acceptances when no train definition or registry entry is in scope.
Code or test changes unrelated to plan artifacts.

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN shape a train's typed id must match; the core's id check, prefer and evidence are expressed against this shape.
The reference form every artifact entry in a train's sequence must match (short domain-and-resource reference, distinct from the artifact's full URN).

proposedKeys.meaning: The reference form for the plan artifacts listed in a train's sequence: a short domain-and-resource reference, distinct from the referenced artifact's full URN.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: Existing urn keys cover each artifact's own URN shape (urn.<artifact>), how a source or test file binds to an artifact (urn.binding.<artifact>), and how a plan artifact declares its own URN (urn.declaration, e.g. wmbt:<wagon>:<wmbt_id>). None describes the short reference form used inside a train's sequence entries, which is exactly what this rule validates.

bunOnly.text: Spec-file existence check relies on planner.train.registry (requires edge: validation enforces spec-file existence).
bunOnly.reason: Names the concrete ATDD-Bun rule id and its graph edge; the core states the dependency generically (the train registry convention enforces spec-file existence), and the specific cross-rule wiring is a realization detail.

neutralityNotes: Trains, the train registry, WMBTs and wagons are treated as stack-neutral ATDD plan-model vocabulary (the closed profile vocabulary itself recognizes train/wmbt/wagon as URN artifacts), so the seven checks, the category vocabulary nominal|error|alternate|exception and the activation kinds/terms stay in the core. The only concrete syntaxes were pushed to the profile: the train id shape via urn.train, and the sequence-artifact reference form via the proposed urn.train_sequence_artifact (no existing key fits; it is a short reference, not a full URN, a binding, or a self-declaration). The cross-rule dependency on the train-registry convention is stated generically in core.verification; the ATDD-Bun rule id planner.train.registry and its graph edge remain bunOnly. Core activation facts drop the per-fact notes (the core fact schema has no note field); their semantics are preserved in the verification array (scope and signal precedence).
